text:
Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd
Data Scientist – Analytics, AI/ML & GenAI anywhere? oa pattern and questions ?

Ticketing System
You are building a ticketing system like Jira. Everyone has their own view of the board, based on the projects they are involved in and the priority of their tasks, and every view is powered by a query. When a ticket is updated, its status can change, it can get assigned to someone else, and so on. Some views are affected by the change. Your task is to find which views are affected, using the query behind each view, in as little time as possible, so the update can be sent to the right users.
The views
The board stores its data in database tables. An example schema:
 * tickets: id, status, priority, project, assignee
 * members: id, name, role
 * comments: id, ticket_id, author
This schema is only an example; the tests also use other tables and columns.
The queries
There are n subscribed queries, numbered 1 to n. Each query reads one table and has the form SELECT * FROM <table> WHERE <condition>.
A condition is built from simple equality checks column = value, combined with AND and OR, nested to any depth. For example: status = PENDING AND (region = R1 OR zone = Z1). In this problem such a condition is given to you as a tree: AND and OR are internal nodes, the equality checks are leaves.
The writes
After all queries are given, q writes arrive, each on one table:
 * INSERT: one new row
 * DELETE: one removed row
 * UPDATE: one row changed; you get the old row and the new row
A row is a set of column value pairs. A row may omit columns; an equality check on a column the row does not contain is simply not satisfied.
When is a query affected
A query is affected by a write when the write is on the query's table and the query's result set could change because of the write. You never see the table's contents; the row carried by the write (for UPDATE, the old and the new version) is all you have.

text:
Ticketing System
You are given n subscribed queries. Each query:

Reads from one database table.
Has a condition represented as a binary logic tree.
Uses AND, OR, and equality conditions of the form column = value. Then q database writes arrive. Each write is one of:
INSERT table — one new row.
DELETE table — one removed row.
UPDATE table — old row followed by new row. For each write, find all query IDs whose result set could change.
A query is affected only if:

The write is on the same table as the query.
The condition evaluates to true for at least one row involved in the write. For UPDATE, check both the old and new rows.
Input format First line: n q
For each query: table_name T node 1 node 2 ... node T

Node formats: AND k c1 c2 ... ck OR k c1 c2 ... ck COND column = value

Node 1 is always the root.

For each write: INSERT table_name c column1 value1 column2 value2 ...

For UPDATE, two rows are provided, old first and new second. 3. Important constraints Parameter Constraint Number of queries (10^5) Number of writes (4 \times 10^4) Nodes per query At most 15 Columns per row At most 20 Internal node children 2 or 3

Time limit: 5 seconds.
